taxonomy_mapping_dispositions.reason: The defence was denied primary FRT system, algorithm, training, database and reliability material needed for authorised review until the appellate court ordered production.

An ordinary criminal-discovery pathway existed and was invoked, while the failure was denial of primary FRT material within that route; this materially distinguishes inaccessible primary evidence from absence of an authorised investigative-access pathway.

The FRT result selected the identity shown to witnesses, but two eyewitness identifications preceded charge; the record therefore materially illuminates the boundary without establishing either inference-only authority or successful independent separation.

evidence_gaps: VIGIL does not describe Arteaga as wrongfully arrested, wrongfully detained or factually misidentified on the basis of the appellate opinion.

The NYPD RTCC result was described as a possible match and was followed by two eyewitness identifications before Arteaga was charged; this prevents VIGIL from treating the facial-recognition inference as independently sufficient arrest authority.

The appellate ruling concerns discovery and the defendant's ability to test the reliability and evidentiary significance of the FRT process; it does not determine the correctness of the match or the final criminal merits.

The earlier AIID characterisation of prolonged pretrial detention is not used for Harm Impact because the reviewed authoritative occurrence evidence does not establish its duration or causal relationship to the FRT process.
